html:
Libya is a large, mostly desert country in North Africa between Egypt and Tunisia. The map shows it in 1914 and 1938 and from 1960. Its three historic regions are Tripolitania, Cyrenaica and the Fezzan.

Italy took the coast from the Ottomans in the Italo-Turkish War of 1911. Conquering the interior took twenty years. The Senussi resistance in Cyrenaica, led by Omar Mukhtar, was crushed with concentration camps in which tens of thousands died. In 1934 the colonies were joined as Italian Libya, and Italian farmers were settled there. In the Second World War the desert war swept back and forth along the coast.

Libya became independent in 1951 as a kingdom under Idris, head of the Senussi order. Oil was found in 1959 and made it rich. In 1969 a young officer, Muammar Gaddafi, overthrew the king. He ruled for 42 years, nationalised the oil industry, backed armed groups abroad and faced Western sanctions. In 2011, during the Arab Spring, a revolt with NATO air support overthrew and killed him. The country then split between rival governments.
